beats.say: India has rights over more than two million square kilometres of sea.
It's called an Exclusive Economic Zone, or EEZ.
A UN treaty lets it reach two hundred nautical miles out.
beats.cap: UN Law of the Sea: up to 200 nautical miles

beats.say: That's about three hundred and seventy kilometres.
India has rights to fish, oil and minerals. Ships can still pass.
beats.cap: Fish · oil · minerals. Ships can still pass

beats.say: Why so big? Islands get zones too.
Andaman and Nicobar add about six hundred thousand square kilometres.
Lakshadweep adds about four hundred thousand. Nearly half, from under one per cent of India's land.
beats.cap: Lakshadweep: ~400,000 km² · nearly half the zone

beats.say: Specks of land, stretching India's sea past two million square kilometres.
beats.cap: Specks of land → 2 million+ km² of sea
